subject: Food Science
title: What Is a Food Additive?
description: A quick win: understand What Is a Food Additive?.

hook.text: Read a label: citric acid, xanthan gum, sodium benzoate. Chemicals everywhere—but what do they actually do?

buildup.text: A food additive is any substance added intentionally to food for a technical purpose—not nutrition.

discovery.text: Additives preserve shelf life, improve texture, enhance color, boost flavor, or fortify nutrition.

twist.text: Many 'chemical-sounding' additives are natural. Citric acid comes from lemons. Lecithin comes from soybeans.

climax.text: Without additives, bread would go stale in hours and peanut butter would separate into oil and sludge.

punchline.text: Additives sound scary. Most just keep your food from falling apart.
